items.name: HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules
items.scope: Protects patient health information (PHI); governs use, disclosure, security safeguards, and breach notification.
items.notes: Applies to covered entities and business associates handling US patient data.

items.name: HITECH Act breach notification requirements
items.scope: Requires notification of patients/HHS/media after a breach of unsecured PHI.
items.notes: Operates alongside HIPAA; breach thresholds and timelines apply.

items.name: GDPR — special category (health) data
items.scope: Health data is a special category requiring an explicit legal basis (e.g. explicit consent, healthcare provision) and stronger safeguards.
items.notes: Applies whenever an EU/EEA data subject's health data is processed, regardless of where the operator is based.

provenance.notes: Cited against the GDPR regulation text itself (authoritative), cross-referenced only loosely with the domain sources; confidence kept medium pending legal review.

items.name: 42 CFR Part 2 — substance use disorder record confidentiality
items.scope: Extra confidentiality protections for records of federally-assisted substance use disorder treatment, stricter than baseline HIPAA.
items.notes: Relevant only to practices offering SUD treatment; access-policy-level segmentation is typically how systems implement this.

provenance.notes: Single-source reasoned inference connecting Medplum's AccessPolicy pattern to this regulation's segmentation requirement.

items.name: ONC Cures Act Final Rule — information blocking
items.scope: Prohibits practices that unreasonably restrict patient access to their electronic health information; drives patient-portal and API access requirements.
items.notes: Motivates providing patients timely electronic access to notes, results, and records.

items.name: HITRUST CSF
items.scope: Security/privacy control framework commonly required by US health-data business partners; harmonizes HIPAA and other standards.
items.notes: Certification, not a legal requirement; often demanded contractually.

items.name: Cross-state/cross-border telehealth licensure
items.scope: A practitioner generally must be licensed in the patient's location to deliver a telehealth visit; interstate compacts vary.
items.notes: Highly jurisdiction-specific; not a single citable rule.

items.name: PCI Data Security Standard
items.scope: Applies to any card payment collected for patient invoicing.
items.notes: Same standard cited across domains handling card payments.
